name: http_get

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: The URL to fetch. Must include the scheme — `https://...` or `http://...`.

returns: A JSON object with `status` (the HTTP status code as a number), `reason` (the [HTTP reason phrase](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9110#name-status-codes), e.g. `"OK"` / `"Not Found"`), and `body` (the response body as a string).
description:
Issue an HTTP `GET` against `url` and return the response as JSON. Synchronous — DuckDB blocks until the response arrives or the request fails.

Extract fields from the result with [DuckDB's JSON operators](https://duckdb.org/docs/data/json/json_functions): `->>` for string fields, `->` for nested JSON. To dive into a JSON response body, cast it: `((http_get(...)->>'body')::JSON)->>'$.field'`.

For REST endpoints that need headers (auth tokens, content negotiation), use [`http_post`](#http_post) instead — `http_get` does not currently expose a headers parameter in the documented signature.

examples.description: Pull a field out of a JSON response body
Per-row enrichment against a REST API
examples.code:
SELECT u.id,
       u.email,
       ((http_get('https://api.example.com/score/' || u.id::VARCHAR)->>'body')::JSON)->>'$.score' AS score
FROM users u
WHERE u.last_seen > now() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR
LIMIT 100;

name: http_post

parameters.name: headers
parameters.description: Request headers as a [`MAP`](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/data_types/map) — `MAP{'authorization': 'Bearer ...', 'content-type': 'application/json'}`. Sent on the wire as-is.

parameters.name: params
parameters.description: Body parameters as a `MAP`. JSON-encoded into the request body — keys become object keys, values become JSON string values.

returns: A JSON object with `status`, `reason`, and `body` — same shape as [`http_get`](#http_get).
description:
Issue an HTTP `POST` with the `params` map JSON-encoded as the request body. Use this for REST APIs that consume JSON; pair it with `headers => MAP{'content-type': 'application/json'}` so the server knows to parse the body as JSON.

For [`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc1866) bodies (older REST APIs, OAuth token endpoints, HTML form handlers), use [`http_post_form`](#http_post_form) instead.

Keep credentials out of cached query plans by binding them through [`SET VARIABLE`](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/statements/set) + [`getenv`](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/functions/utility#getenv) — see [Securing credentials](#technical-details).

examples.description: Authorize with a Bearer token sourced from the environment
Read just the status to verify the call succeeded

name: http_post_form

parameters.name: headers
parameters.description: Request headers as a [`MAP`](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/data_types/map). Pass `MAP{}` if you don't need any.

parameters.name: params
parameters.description: Form fields as a `MAP`. Each entry is URL-encoded into the request body using [`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc1866).

returns: A JSON object with `status`, `reason`, and `body` — same shape as [`http_get`](#http_get).
description:
Issue an HTTP `POST` with the `params` map encoded as [`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc1866) — the body shape used by HTML forms, many older REST APIs, and [OAuth 2.0](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6750) token endpoints.

The extension sets the request's `Content-Type` header to `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` for you; you don't need to put it in `headers` manually.

For JSON request bodies, use [`http_post`](#http_post) instead.

name: http_head

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: The URL to issue the [`HEAD`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Methods/HEAD) request against.

returns: A JSON object with the same `status` / `reason` / `body` shape as [`http_get`](#http_get). For a well-behaved server the body is empty.
description:
Issue an HTTP [`HEAD`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Methods/HEAD) request — same response metadata as a `GET`, but without a body. Use it for liveness checks or to test whether a URL exists before fetching the full payload with [`http_get`](#http_get).

This function is exposed by the extension binary but is **not documented in the upstream [README](https://github.com/Query-farm/duckdb-extension-httpclient)** — the signature could change in a future release. Treat it as best-effort.
